coverage_rule: Required scenarios need valid observations; UNSURE/NOT-TESTED/skipped are incomplete. A task subset does not certify complete parity. Screenshots do not prove real audio.

uses.title: Complete Rune Phase 0 feasibility gate
uses.do: A musician opens Rune on a real project, starts and stops playback, seeks, changes tempo, mutes and adjusts a track, moves a clip, adds a note, and confirms the rendered result. Terra records visible state and engine/audio evidence; screenshots alone do not establish sound. Terra also conducts the specified plug-in-window and Orca checks in an isolated display/session.
uses.expect: All applicable user-visible acceptance criteria hold: Exercise the six prototype surfaces against a real engine and real project; prove engine state and rendered audio with render or engine meter/peak evidence. Report command/ack and subscription latency under load, including p95 and whether optimistic edits reconcile; measure playhead and meters at display rate. Build, open, and run deterministic headless checks on Linux, Windows MSVC, and macOS; separate hosted CI evidence from any local cross-target check. Check native plug-in editor open/focus/close/stacking behavior on Wayland and X11 and obtain platform evidence for Windows and macOS, stating any CI-only limitation. Exercise transport, track list, and mixer with Orca; document evidence and concrete follow-up needs for NVDA and VoiceOver. Deliver explicit GO, NO-GO, or BLOCKED per spike and an overall recommendation; list control-surface gaps for headless-engine operation and audio editing; distinguish removing the Qt window from any later removal of Qt libraries without prescribing speculative bulk/streaming work. Terra reviews the applicable cases from plans/rune-review-scenarios.json on the pinned Rune build. Required cases need observed PASS; missing prerequisites, UNSURE or skipped cases remain incomplete. Preserve independent code review and separately measured platform, latency and audio evidence.

uses.title: Rune engine process lifecycle and connection
uses.do: Launch Rune into a project, close and reopen the UI, then simulate an unavailable engine and a dropped connection. Terra verifies clear status, successful reconnect, and preserved project state.
uses.expect: All applicable user-visible acceptance criteria hold: On supported platforms, Rune opens the engine through the documented control connection and shows a usable project state without creating a Qt window. Connection refusal, engine startup failure, engine exit, UI exit, and reconnect produce actionable status and do not corrupt or silently discard project data. The engine remains independently startable and usable by existing control clients; no new mandatory Qt dependency is introduced into the UI process. Lifecycle and protocol compatibility are covered by deterministic tests and platform CI. Terra reviews the applicable cases from plans/rune-review-scenarios.json on the pinned Rune build. Required cases need observed PASS; missing prerequisites, UNSURE or skipped cases remain incomplete. Preserve independent code review and separately measured platform, latency and audio evidence.

uses.title: Rune accessibility, parity inventory, and adoption gate
uses.do: A musician completes the full first-session journey without coaching on each supported platform, then repeats key transport, track, mixer, and editing actions using keyboard/screen-reader support. Terra records blockers, state/audio evidence, and uncertain or skipped actions for retest.
uses.expect: All applicable user-visible acceptance criteria hold: Keyboard navigation, command/menu discoverability, focus and selection feedback, screen-reader roles/names/states, scaling, and contrast support the first-session journey across supported platforms. Build a traceable inventory from the current advertised feature set, control surface, Qt workflows, and platform support, classifying each as equivalent, owner-accepted deferred, or blocked with evidence. Run complete musician sessions through Terra's centralized human-use review; all findings follow existing independent review, repair budgets, and Terra priority/promotion rules. Performance, startup, interaction latency, memory, packaging, audio, recording, plug-in, and accessibility evidence identify platform and test conditions and compare against budgets established from Phase 0/baseline. uses.title: Focus keyboard
uses.do: Navigate all active regions with keyboard only; move focus into and out of a modal, close it with Escape, then return to the previous editor.
uses.expect: Focus is visible, logical and restored; selection and playback do not change accidentally; no trap or hidden focused control.

uses.title: Text shortcuts
uses.do: Rename an item and edit a numeric field with selection, arrows, Delete, undo, clipboard and non-ASCII/IME input; type keys that are also music shortcuts.
uses.expect: Text/IME editing stays in the field; transport and project shortcuts do not fire; Enter commits and Escape cancels as documented without losing prior data.

uses.title: Selection targets
uses.do: Select one item then multiple items; open a context menu on a different item, switch panels and inspect mixed values.
uses.expect: The command target and selected set are unambiguous; mixed values are marked mixed; multi-edits preserve offsets and do not silently affect incompatible items.

uses.title: Drag cancel
uses.do: Preview move/resize, cross a snap boundary, cancel with Escape and try an invalid drop. Then make the same edit using a non-drag alternative.
uses.expect: Cancel leaves the original unchanged; invalid drops explain refusal and preserve data; a completed gesture is one undo step; alternative paths produce the same result.

uses.title: Precision control
uses.do: Adjust a fader or numeric value with normal and fine pointer movement, type an exact value, try invalid text, reset it, undo and redo.
uses.expect: Units/range/default are clear; pointer, keys and exact entry agree; invalid input is explained without silent coercion; undo restores the original and redo the edited value.

uses.title: Undo roundtrip
uses.do: Make a known edit, undo it, redo it, save, close and reopen; compare object identities, positions and musical content.
uses.expect: Undo and redo restore the exact intended state; reopening preserves the committed content and does not duplicate an edit or lose objects.

uses.title: Async recovery
uses.do: Exercise a slow operation, cancellation and an unavailable or disconnected engine with appropriate test fixtures; attempt a reasonable recovery.
uses.expect: Pending differs from completed; busy state stays responsive; failure/cancel is truthful; retry does not duplicate work; acknowledged data is preserved and recovery is actionable.

uses.title: Files errors
uses.do: Save/open/export using spaces and Unicode paths; cancel, try read-only/missing paths, then recover through the UI.
uses.expect: Dialog keyboard flow and overwrite protection work; errors identify the action and next step; cancellation creates no misleading success or unwanted file.

uses.title: Window focus
uses.do: Open a native plug-in editor, switch focus, edit a plug-in field, close and reopen it, and return to the Rune editor on each claimed window system.
uses.expect: Editor focus/z-order/close are correct; typing does not trigger Rune shortcuts; returning restores useful focus; errors do not freeze engine or UI.

uses.title: Scaling accessibility
uses.do: Use keyboard, a real screen reader, enlarged scaling and high contrast across transport, tracks, editor and mixer; scroll and resize.
uses.expect: Roles/names/values and disabled states are announced; labels and hit targets remain usable and unclipped; state does not depend only on color or hover; no undiscoverable required operation.

uses.title: Solo comparator
uses.do: Create TWO sounding tracks with distinguishable content, route them correctly, then compare mute/solo/fader/bypass changes.
uses.expect: The intended signal changes and other signal is preserved/silenced as expected; do not declare solo verified without a second sounding comparator and independent output evidence.

uses.title: Zoom tooltip
uses.do: Zoom and scroll around a selected edit, hover unfamiliar controls, then reach the same help and edit using keyboard.
uses.expect: Zoom anchor and selection remain predictable; hit targets match visible geometry; tooltips do not steal focus or hide essential content and are not the only source of required information.
